# Fix inherited_pass bypass: three fixes in audit_runner.py

## Summary
The audit runner incorrectly allows `inherited_pass` to bypass the pre-review stage block, producing false-positive "Ready to close: Yes" verdicts. This task combines three related fixes in `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`.

## Fix 1: inherited_pass assignment (line ~9897)

In the `if not parent_gaps:` branch, add a stage guard so `inherited_pass=True` is only applied to children already in `in_review` or `done` stage. Pre-review children (`idea`, `intake_complete`, `plan_complete`) must not receive `inherited_pass` — they must be audited independently.

- Code at ~9897 checks child stage before setting `inherited_pass = True`
- Only children with `stage` in `("in_review", "done")` receive `inherited_pass`
- Pre-review stage children skip the `inherited_pass` branch and proceed to independent audit
- Existing `_child_content_changed` guard is preserved

## Fix 2: all_children_reviewed check (line ~4207)

The `all_children_reviewed` check currently allows `inherited_pass` to exempt a child from the stage check:

```python
all_children_reviewed = all(
    c.get("stage") in ("in_review", "done") or c.get("inherited_pass")
    for c in active_children
)
```

Remove `or c.get("inherited_pass")` — the stage check should be independent. The `inherited_pass` flag affects the verdict, not the stage blocking logic.

- `all_children_reviewed` only checks child stages, not `inherited_pass`
- A child at `intake_complete` with `inherited_pass=True` is correctly counted as blocking
- Existing exempt-child logic (deleted, completed/done) is preserved

## Fix 3: summary text (line ~4333)

The summary unconditionally appends "All children are in in_review or done stage." when `all_children_reviewed` is true. Fix this so the line is only emitted when that statement is actually true; otherwise, the summary names the blocking children.

- The "All children are in in_review or done stage." line is only emitted when all active children are actually in those stages
- When children block closure, the summary names them
- No regression on existing "Ready to close: No" cases that already name blocking children

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All three fixes applied in `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`
- [ ] Regression test passes (separate task SA-0MUD5OMQG0068P4I)
- [ ] No regression on existing tests
- [ ] Existing `_child_content_changed` guard preserved
- [ ] Existing exempt-child logic preserved

**Key Files:**
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` (~4201-4214, ~4330-4340, ~9890-9910)

# [TEST] Stale-ctx regression tests for pi-client extensions

## Goal

As a Pi extension maintainer, I want regression tests that inject a **stale
`ExtensionContext`** (after a session replacement/reload) into the
`proxy-compaction-bridge` and `proxy-sse-signals` extension logic, so a stale
ctx can never crash an unrelated run and the fix is proven red-before-green.

Parent: **SA-0MUEIOGT2005IR7F**. Covers parent AC2 (stale-ctx-safe extensions)
and AC4 (Node-side regression tests that fail against pre-fix code).

## Scope

- Add `node:test` coverage that injects a stale-ctx stub whose `ui` /
  `sessionManager` accessors **throw** the pi stale-ctx error, then assert the
  extension's handler/callback behaviour is a safe no-op / context passthrough
  rather than a throw.
- Follow the existing pure-module architecture: the guard/decision helper must
  live in the dependency-free JS core (`compaction-bridge.js`,
  `sse-signals.js`) so it is importable by `tests/unit/**/*.mjs` (node v22
  cannot import the `.ts` adapters directly).
- These tests are expected to **fail against pre-fix code** (red). They will be
  made green by the two hardening implementation items.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `tests/unit/test_compaction-bridge.mjs` contains a case that injects a
   stale-ctx stub (getter throws on `sessionManager`/`ui` access) and asserts
   the bridge's session-scoped handling does not throw and degrades to a safe
   no-op (documented expected result).
- `tests/unit/test-proxy-sse-signals.mjs` contains a case that injects a
   stale-ctx stub for the captured UI handle and asserts the status path does
   not throw (status write skipped/no-op).
- Running `node --test "tests/unit/**/*.mjs"` at the pre-fix commit shows the
   new cases **failing** (red evidence recorded in a work-item comment), while
   all pre-existing cases still pass.
- The new tests assert observable behaviour (no throw + no state mutation / no
   UI call), not implementation internals.

## Minimal Implementation

- Import the (new or existing) pure helper from the extension `.js` core and
  drive it with a stale-ctx stub.
- If the guard helper does not yet exist, add the test against the intended
  helper API first (red), then let the implementation item add it.

## Dependencies

- None (test-first: this item precedes the two hardening implementation items).

## Deliverables

- Added stale-ctx cases in both `tests/unit` test files.
- Red-run evidence comment on this item.

**Key Files:**
- `tests/unit/test_compaction-bridge.mjs`
- `tests/unit/test-proxy-sse-signals.mjs`
- `pi-client/proxy-compaction-bridge/compaction-bridge.js`
- `pi-client/proxy-sse-signals/sse-signals.js`

# [IMPL] Harden proxy-compaction-bridge against stale ctx

## Goal

As a Pi extension maintainer, I want `proxy-compaction-bridge` to no-op when
the captured `ctx` has been invalidated by a session replacement, so its
handlers never throw `This extension ctx is stale ...` and never crash or
degrade an unrelated run.

Parent: **SA-0MUEIOGT2005IR7F**. Covers parent AC2 and part of AC5.

## Scope

- `pi-client/proxy-compaction-bridge/index.ts`: both the
  `after_provider_response` and `context` handlers call
  `ctx.sessionManager.getSessionId()` — a stale ctx throws.
- Move the session-id resolution into a stale-safe helper in the dependency-free
  core `compaction-bridge.js` (e.g. `safeSessionId(ctx)` returning `null` when
  access throws). The adapter must:
  - `after_provider_response`: no-op when the session id cannot be resolved.
  - `context`: return `undefined` (pass through messages unchanged) when the
    session id cannot be resolved.
- Never let a stale-ctx throw escape a handler; never mutate dispatch on an
  unknown session.
- Update `docs/dev/proxy-compaction-bridge.md` to document the stale-ctx
  fail-safe behaviour.
- Preserve the compaction-bridge wire contract (LP-0MTYGZ1DI0004QP8) and the
  existing dispatch reshape semantics exactly.

## Acceptance Criteria

- With a stale-ctx stub, both handlers do not throw; `context` returns
   `undefined` (passthrough) and `after_provider_response` performs no state
   update.
- With a live ctx, behaviour is byte-for-byte unchanged (existing
   compaction/reshape tests continue to pass, wire contract intact).
- `docs/dev/proxy-compaction-bridge.md` documents the stale-ctx fail-safe
   path and this work item.
- The stale-ctx regression tests added by the test item pass (green).

## Minimal Implementation

- Add `safeSessionId(ctx)` (try/catch around `ctx.sessionManager.getSessionId()`)
  to `compaction-bridge.js` and export it.
- Use it in the two `index.ts` handlers with early return.
- Add the docs paragraph.

## Dependencies

- Depends on **[TEST] Stale-ctx regression tests for pi-client extensions**.

## Deliverables

- Stale-safe `proxy-compaction-bridge` handlers.
- Documented fail-safe behaviour.
- Green stale-ctx regression tests.

**Key Files:**
- `pi-client/proxy-compaction-bridge/index.ts`
- `pi-client/proxy-compaction-bridge/compaction-bridge.js`
- `tests/unit/test_compaction-bridge.mjs`
- `docs/dev/proxy-compaction-bridge.md`

# [IMPL] Harden proxy-sse-signals against stale ctx

## Goal

As a Pi extension maintainer, I want `proxy-sse-signals` to no-op when its
captured UI handle (`statusUi`) belongs to an invalidated ctx, so a
session-replacement cannot make its async capturing-fetch callback throw and
crash or degrade an unrelated run.

Parent: **SA-0MUEIOGT2005IR7F**. Covers parent AC2 and part of AC5.

## Scope

- `pi-client/proxy-sse-signals/index.ts`: `turn_start` captures
  `ctx.hasUI ? ctx.ui : null`; the capturing-fetch callback later calls
  `statusUi.setStatus(...)` and `turn_end` calls `ctx.ui.setStatus(...)` — both
  can hit a stale ctx/UI handle.
- Add a stale-safe status helper in the dependency-free core `sse-signals.js`
  (e.g. `safeSetStatus(ui, key, text)` that swallows/guards stale-ctx throws
  and reports whether the write happened) and use it from the adapter so a
  stale handle is a silent no-op.
- `turn_end` must not throw when the ctx/UI is stale; clearing the local handle
  must still occur.
- Preserve SSE signal parsing/formatting behaviour and the passthrough of bytes
  through the capturing fetch unchanged.
- Update `pi-client/proxy-sse-signals/README.md` (or code comments) to document
  the stale-ctx fail-safe behaviour.

## Acceptance Criteria

- With a stale-ctx stub, the captured-status path and `turn_end` do not throw;
   the status write is skipped and the local handle is cleared.
- With a live ctx, signal rendering behaviour is unchanged (existing
   `sse-signals` tests pass; bytes still pass through unwrapped).
- Stale-ctx fail-safe behaviour is documented in the extension README/comments
   with a reference to this work item.
- The stale-ctx regression tests added by the test item pass (green).

## Minimal Implementation

- Add `safeSetStatus(ui, key, text)` to `sse-signals.js` and export it.
- Use it in `index.ts` for both the callback and `turn_end`; always clear the
  captured handle in `turn_end`.
- Add the docs note.

## Dependencies

- Depends on **[TEST] Stale-ctx regression tests for pi-client extensions**.

## Deliverables

- Stale-safe `proxy-sse-signals` status handling.
- Documented fail-safe behaviour.
- Green stale-ctx regression tests.

**Key Files:**
- `pi-client/proxy-sse-signals/index.ts`
- `pi-client/proxy-sse-signals/sse-signals.js`
- `pi-client/proxy-sse-signals/README.md`
- `tests/unit/test-proxy-sse-signals.mjs`

As a release manager, I want evidence that an audit pi call that triggers a

unblocked and the fix is proven end-to-end.

## Summary

Fix `_build_file_scope_manifest()` so the Phase 2 FILE SCOPE manifest includes the audited item's committed touched files (via the existing `_resolve_touched_files()`), not just working-tree changes. This is the production fix for parent SA-0MUJNZ5RN0078B5M.

## Target outcome

On a clean checkout of a fully-committed item, the manifest covers the item's real changed files, so Phase 2 no longer returns false "outside the manifest" verdicts.

## Definition of done

- `_build_file_scope_manifest()` calls `_resolve_touched_files(runner, issue_id, work_item=issue)` (reusing the already-fetched item) and adds a manifest section listing those paths.
- Paths are de-duplicated against the existing changed-files / Key Files entries; the total listed files respect `_FILE_SCOPE_MAX_FILES`.
- Fail-open: when `_resolve_touched_files` returns `None`, the manifest degrades gracefully to the existing sections (Key Files / Phase 1 refs / repo index).
- All C1 regression tests pass; existing manifest tests still pass.
- Docs: update `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` (FILE SCOPE manifest description) and `skill/audit/SKILL.md` where the manifest composition is described, to state it now includes the item's committed touched files.

## Minimal implementation

1. Call `_resolve_touched_files` inside `_build_file_scope_manifest`.
2. Emit a new `Touched files (from item commits):` manifest section (alongside `Changed files`).
3. Merge, de-duplicate, and cap at `_FILE_SCOPE_MAX_FILES`.

## Constraints

- Do not change verdict semantics; scope expansion is additive only, bounded to avoid context growth.
- Fail-open on any git failure (never raise from the manifest builder).
- Preserve determinism: pass the already-fetched item so the grep + Key Files sources are consistent at audit and freshness-check time.

## Risky assumptions

- `_resolve_touched_files` is cheap enough (one `git log` call) to run during manifest build.
- The call site has the fetched `issue` (it does: `_build_file_scope_manifest(issue, ac_results, runner=runner)`).

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_build_file_scope_manifest`, `_resolve_touched_files`
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_phase2.py`
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `_build_file_scope_manifest()` includes the item's committed touched files (via `_resolve_touched_files()`) in addition to the working-tree diff, Key Files, Phase 1 refs, and repo index.
- [ ] Paths are de-duplicated and the manifest respects `_FILE_SCOPE_MAX_FILES`.
- [ ] When touched-file resolution returns `None`, the manifest is still built without error.
- [ ] `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` documents the new manifest source.
- [ ] C1 regression tests pass and existing manifest tests remain green.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by C1 (test-first).
data.title: Include committed touched files in FILE SCOPE manifest

## Summary

Ensure the fail-fast scope validation cannot accept a manifest that references the item repo but omits the item's touched files. After C2 the builder includes touched files, so such a manifest should be impossible to build for a resolvable item; this item adds the regression test and (recommended) a defensive validator check.

## Target outcome

A regression test proves an item-repo-referencing manifest that omits the item's touched files is rejected (or cannot be built), and the validator fails closed when touched files are resolvable but absent from the manifest.

## Decision (producer, 2026-09-27)

**Harden** `_validate_file_scope_manifest()`: add an optional `touched_files` parameter that returns a scope error when a non-empty resolved touched set has no path in the manifest, and fails open when the set is `None`/empty. The regression test is still required.

## Definition of done

- Regression test: given a resolvable touched-file set and a manifest that references the item repo but contains none of those files, validation returns an error — or the test proves the builder always includes them.
- `_validate_file_scope_manifest(file_scope, owning_root, touched_files=None)` returns an error only when `touched_files` is non-empty and none appear in the manifest; `None`/empty → fail-open (preserves behaviour for mono-repo / unknown cases).
- Both call sites in `audit_runner.py` pass the resolved touched set.
- Existing `TestFileScopeManifestValidation` tests still pass.

## Constraints

- Fail-open when the touched set cannot be determined — never block a legitimately-launched audit.
- Do not regress the existing inclusion-based top-level-marker check.

## Risky assumptions

- The touched-file set is resolvable at validation time (it is: `_resolve_touched_files` exists and C2 uses it).
- Hardening will not false-positive on mono-repo items (touched paths appear in the manifest after C2).

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_validate_file_scope_manifest` and its call sites
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_launch_context.py`
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_phase2.py`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A scope-validation regression test asserts an item-repo-referencing manifest that omits the item's touched files is rejected (or is provably impossible to build).
- [ ] The validator fails closed only when a non-empty touched set has no manifest entry; `None`/empty fails open.
- [ ] Both validation call sites pass the resolved touched set.
- [ ] Existing file-scope validation tests remain green.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by C2.
data.title: Harden scope validation against omitted touched files

## Goal

Invert the existing `TestLaunchContextGuard` abort-on-mismatch tests so they assert that a determinable non-owning cwd launch proceeds (with a one-line stderr warning) and that only undeterminable ownership aborts with zero git commands and zero pi calls.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `test_non_owning_cwd_aborts_with_zero_pi_calls` is rewritten to assert that a non-owning cwd proceeds (rc == 0, pi calls are made) and that a one-line stderr warning naming launch vs owning root is emitted.
2. `test_non_owning_cwd_error_names_resolved_vs_expected` is rewritten: no more `Audit launch-context error` — instead assert the stderr contains a warning with both roots.

7. `TestGitResolutionFromNonOwningCwd` tests are extended to assert that the per-audit root is threaded correctly to all consumers (code-quality scan, debug-log dir, remediation loop, F3 suite-execution cwd).
